title: Change the blade in a butterfly safety razor, holding the blade only by its edges
instruction: Put the new blade into the butterfly razor so it sits on the posts under the closed doors, then let go.
context: Anyone who wet-shaves with a double-edge safety razor changes the blade every few shaves, and barbers do it between customers. The razor's doors open by twisting its handle knob, the blade goes on over two locating posts, and the doors close on it. The blade's two long sides are cutting edges that slice a fingertip, so it is only ever held by its short ends. The robot has to twist the knob with one hand and keep it turned while the other hand carries and seats a 43 mm steel blade 0.4 mm thick.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475; heights below are above the table top. (1) Razor stand, fixed to the table at (0.240, 0.000): a 70 x 70 x 35 mm base, dark steel (0.18, 0.19, 0.21), friction 0.6; with the handle and head plate, 0.8 kg. (2) Handle: a 12 mm steel cylinder from 35 to 126 mm, silver (0.75, 0.77, 0.80). (3) Head plate: 34 x 27 x 4 mm chrome steel, top at 130 mm, silver; two posts of 2.8 mm diameter and 1.6 mm height at x = +-8 mm from the plate centre, on its centre line. (4) Two doors: 34 x 10.5 x 1.2 mm chrome steel, 3.3 g each, friction 0.5, hinged along x at y = +-12.5 mm from the plate centre, on the plate top; closed, each lies 0.6 mm above the plate over y 2 to 12.5 mm (a 4 mm slit over the posts); open to 100 deg, standing 1.5 mm outside each of the blade's long sides. (5) Knob: a 22 mm diameter, 12 mm tall black steel cylinder, 30 g, friction 1.0, on the handle with its centre 46 mm up, turning about the vertical handle axis; clockwise seen from above, 0 to 100 deg, with a 0.01 N m/rad return spring to 0 and 0.0005 N m friction. A cam turns the doors with it: 90 deg of knob turn opens the doors to 100 deg. (6) Blade: a double-edge razor blade, 43 x 22 x 0.4 mm steel, 3 g, light silver (0.86, 0.87, 0.90), friction 1.0, with two 4.4 mm square holes centred at x = +-8 mm; its long sides (the outer 3 mm) are the cutting edges. It lies flat, long axis along x, centred at (0.240, -0.120), 130.2 mm up, on the shelf. (7) Blade shelf: a 26 x 14 mm shelf on a 130 mm post on a 60 x 60 x 12 mm base, blue anodised aluminium (0.30, 0.45, 0.65), 0.5 kg, fixed at (0.240, -0.120); the blade's short ends overhang the shelf by 8.5 mm. No object jitter.
scoring: Whole-run record (a linkkit History updated every control step, cleared only by the simulator reset). Measured in the head frame (mm from the plate centre; dz from the plate top): dx, dy, dz of the blade's centre, its yaw and tilt, the door angles, the knob angle, each gripper's opening and pad clearance. Gate, any time in the run, gives 0: a gripper pad (12 mm wide footprint) within 1 mm of a flat face of the blade over its outer 3 mm (the cutting edges, |y| from 8 mm to 11 mm). Otherwise the best rung: 0.25 = the blade held by a gripper and 20 mm or more above the shelf while both doors are open 60 deg or more; 0.5 = the blade seated (centre within 1.5 mm in x and y of the plate centre, gap under it at most 0.6 mm, yaw at most 5 deg, tilt at most 3 deg) while the doors are open 60 deg or more; 0.75 = at the end the blade seated, both doors at most 2 deg from closed, knob at most 15 deg from 0; 1.0 = also the blade still (under 1 mm/s and 2 deg/s) for 1 s, and the release gate: every pad point of both grippers 30 mm or more from the blade and razor and both grippers moving under 10 mm/s for 1 s. Real trial: the blade's two long edges are inked with washable blue marker and each gripper pad is taped with white paper tape; any blue on a tape is a touch (0). Heights and angles are read from a top photo with a mm scale and a side video on a 20 Hz clock: the doors are read by protractor; the gap under the blade by a 0.7 mm feeler leaf that must not slide under it; a door is closed if a 0.5 mm leaf does not slide between its free edge and the blade; the knob by the index mark on it; lift by the shelf's scale in the video; clearance by a 30 mm gauge block.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Open the knob, take the blade out by its short ends with tweezers, lay it back on the shelf with its long axis along x and its near short end overhanging the shelf (centred on (0.240, -0.120)), re-ink its two long edges, and put fresh white tape on both pads. Let the knob spring back to 0 and check the doors lie flat (a 0.5 mm leaf does not slide under a door's free edge). The stand and shelf are fixed on taped outlines and need no reset.
fidelity: The doors follow the knob through a software cam (a real razor uses a gear or cam); the knob turns 90 deg and springs back, which real razors do not. The blade is 0.4 mm thick and 3 g (real 0.1 mm, 0.8 g) so the solver holds it; holes are two squares, with no centre slot. The pad footprint is taken as 12 mm. Stand and shelf are rigid and fixed.
